narrative.overview:
The dashboard reads the host app's runtime the way a rider reads a network map. Each event kind is a line with a fixed colour, every log row carries the station marker of its line, and a trace is a route drawn stop by stop from the incoming request to wherever it failed. The shell is a navy signage band; the ground is a white map in light theme and a navy night map in dark. Red appears only where service is disrupted.

Density is operational, built for someone reading next to an editor: 38px rows, 34px controls, a 14px body, and panels that sit flat on the ground behind 1px rules. Hierarchy comes from weight in Overpass, a signage sans, far more than from size; its sibling Overpass Mono carries everything a developer copies or compares. The form language is the map's own: thick round-capped strokes, ring stations, interchange dots for status, and branches that leave their parent line at 45 degrees.

Both themes are complete: every colour token has a light and a dark value, and the theme is set before first paint from the saved choice or the OS. Motion is spent once, on drawing a trace's route; everything else is short state feedback. The system rejects the category default it replaced: a grey slate dashboard of KPI cards with one neon accent.
keyCharacteristics: A fixed line palette with one colour per event kind, mirrored for each theme.
Red reserved for disruption, amber for delay, green for good service, blue washes for information.
A 56px navy signage band whose tabs are underlined in their own line colours.
Flat panels with 1px rules; shadows only on what floats over the map.
Overpass for words, Overpass Mono for ids, times, paths and measurements.
Ring stations, interchange status dots, 45-degree branches, round caps throughout.
One authored motion: the route draws itself when a trace opens.

rules.name: The Disruption Red Rule
rules.body: Red means something failed. No line is red, errors ride Disruption Red instead of a line, and a solid red fill appears only on failed stops, error stations, the CRITICAL chip, and status dots at severe or unreachable. A new use of red needs a failure behind it.

rules.name: The One Kind, One Line Rule
rules.body: An event kind keeps its line colour everywhere it appears: table station, route segment, waterfall bar, inspector badge. A new kind gets its own `--l-*` pair, light and dark, before it ships; it never borrows a state colour or a neighbour's line.

rules.name: The Lifted Band Rule
rules.body: On the navy band, colour comes only from the band variants (Band Blue, Red, Green, Violet, Amber) and the band neutrals, never from the ground-map line or state values.

rules.name: The Mono Is Measurement Rule
rules.body: Overpass Mono is for what a developer copies or compares: ids, timestamps, paths, durations, methods, status codes, signatures, axis ticks, payloads. Labels, headings and sentences stay in Overpass, even inside a mono column; the waterfall's "Duration" header switches back. All table cells, stat figures, counts, trace facts and tooltip values use tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Weight Ladder Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy steps by weight (400, 500, 600, 650, 700, 750, 800) inside a narrow 10.5px to 26px band. Nothing is set larger than 26px, and tracking tightens to -0.01em only at 17px and above.

rules.name: The Optical Drop Rule
rules.body: Overpass sits high in its line box, so text beside a marker drops onto the optical centre: station labels take 2px of top padding, chips 1px, tabs 2px.

rules.name: The Continuous Line Rule
rules.body: Trace rows are exactly 38px tall and each route drawing is 38px with its stop at 19px, so one row's line meets the next row's without a seam. Changing the row height breaks the route.

rules.name: The Reserved Inspector Rule
rules.body: From 1200px up, opening the inspector takes its width out of the page instead of covering the list, so the rows stay readable and walkable with J and K while an event is open.

rules.name: The Flat Map Rule
rules.body: Anything that belongs to the map (panels, table, lists, cards, the lock card) sits flat with a 1px Hairline border. Only what floats over the map casts a shadow, and that shadow is always offset and softly blurred.

rules.name: The Ring and Fill Rule
rules.body: A station is a ring: line-coloured stroke around a Panel-coloured centre. A solid fill marks state: a failed station or stop fills Disruption Red, a warning stop fills Delay Amber, and the active tab fills its ring. Log events inside a route are the one exception, drawn as small solid ticks (3.5px radius) on their span's line, not as stations.

rules.name: The Interchange Rule
rules.body: Status is drawn as an interchange: a solid dot, a gap in the colour of whatever it sits on, and a ring of the same colour. The band status dot uses 10px with 2px gap and ring; the disruption count uses 12px with 2px; the Metrics line status uses 18px with 3px. Only service status and error counts use this form.

rules.name: The 45-Degree Branch Rule
rules.body: Lines change direction only at 45 degrees, with equal run and rise: in the mark, in the empty-state route, and wherever a child event branches off its parent in a trace. Nothing curves.

dos: Do take every colour from a custom property declared on both `:root` and `[data-theme="dark"]`; both themes ship finished.
Do give a new event kind its own `--l-*` line pair and show it as a ring station with a text label.
Do pair a state's wash with its ink (Disruption, Delay, Good, Info) for chips, banners and rows, and keep solid Disruption Red for failed stops, error stations and CRITICAL.
Do keep map panels flat: Panel fill, 1px Hairline border, 10px radius, 12 to 16px vertical and 16 to 18px horizontal padding, stacked 12px apart.
Do carry state in words as well as colour: the status dot travels with its status text, level chips spell the level, failed traces say "Has errors".
Do state empty and degraded conditions plainly: the empty-route drawing, a 15px Ink title, one Muted sentence; queued and dropped counts in the band whenever they are above zero.
Do keep the route draw as the only entrance animation, on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`, and make every motion resolve to its final state under reduced motion.
Do draw icons as 24-grid stroke SVGs at 16px: 2px stroke, round caps and joins, `currentColor`, no fill.
donts: Don't use red, or any colour from the Disruption family, for anything that did not fail.
Don't put ground-map line or state colours on the navy band; use the band variants.
Don't shadow a panel that sits on the map, and never use a shadow without blur.
Don't split the metrics into separate KPI cards; the five figures share one ruled strip.
Don't set labels or sentences in Overpass Mono, and don't set type larger than 26px.
Don't curve a route or a branch; lines turn at 45 degrees.
Don't change trace row height from 38px without redrawing the route geometry to match.
Don't load fonts, icons or scripts from the network; Overpass and Overpass Mono ship as local woff2 files.
Don't add hard-coded colours; the band amber, its ink, the band hover and badge whites, and the CRITICAL chip ink are existing literals, not a pattern to copy.
